land.text: Iran as the last Pahlavi shape drew it (Cliopatria 1,624,335 km2)

predecessors.note: The Iranian Revolution is dated 11 February 1979 and the republic 1 April 1979 (Iran page); Cliopatria's Pahlavi row ends in 1978 and this one starts in 1979, the same outline.

rulers.name: Ruhollah Khomeini
rulers.title: Supreme Leader
rulers.note: 'Khomeini became Supreme Leader in December 1979'; leader of the revolution from February 1979; the page says he was on his deathbed in 1989 and gives no date of death.

rulers.name: Ali Khamenei
rulers.title: Supreme Leader
rulers.note: Named by the 25-man Constitutional Reform Council in 1989; the page says he was assassinated on 28 February 2026, after the map's last year.

keyframe_review.note: 1,624,310 km2 for 1979-1982 against the infobox 1,648,195 km2 (ratio 0.985): the same outline Cliopatria gives the Pahlavi state and the 1990 shape, a raster of the present frontier. It is the right shape for the state's core; the Iraqi invasion of 22 September 1980 and the Kurdish rebellion are carried by the ledger's contest events, not by this shape.

correction.text: Iran within its 1979 frontier; the five cells the 1983-1986 shape adds beyond that outline (four at 30.64-30.98 N, 47.81-48.07 E east of Basra and one of the eastern frontier shifted at 33.7 N, 60.5 E) are not Iranian territory: Iranian-held Iraqi land of these years is drawn by the ledger's occupation events (Haj Omran from July 1983, Majnoon Island from February 1984, al-Faw from February 1986)

keyframe_review.note: 1,624,878 km2 against 1,624,310 for 1979: five cells (about 1,264 km2) are not in the 1979 outline, four of them on the Iraqi side east of Basra (a gazetteer comparison). The war page dates the Iranian gains of these years: part of the Bayat oilfield in November 1982, Haj Omran on 23 July 1983 (now a ledger event), 'some Iraqi land' in Operation Dawn 4 and Majnoon Island by 27 February 1984. None of them is east of Basra: the ground there (Fish Lake, within 15 km of the city) is the Karbala-5 gain of January 1987 (Operation Karbala-5 page), so the four 1983 cells match no page and are probably Cliopatria placing the 1987 front early; they are removed. The war page says 'The war did not create any permanent border changes', so land held in war is occupation, not territory. Infobox ratio 0.985.

correction.text: Iran within its 1979 frontier; the nine cells the 1987-1989 shape adds beyond it (six at 30.64-30.98 N, 47.70-48.07 E east of Basra and three at 36.05-36.24 N, 45.14-45.37 E in Iraqi Kurdistan) are Iranian-held Iraqi land, drawn as occupation by the ledger (Karbala-5 east of Basra from January 1987 and Karbala-10 in Iraqi Kurdistan from April 1987) and not as Iranian territory

keyframe_review.note: 1,626,457 km2, the largest of the seven shapes: nine cells (about 2,276 km2) beyond the 1990 outline, none of them in the 1990 shape (the first version said seven plus three; the gazetteer comparison gives six plus three). Six cells at 30.64-30.98 N, 47.70-48.07 E are the ground Iran took east of Basra in Operation Karbala-5 (8 January 1987, Fish Lake, the Duayji canal, within 15 km of Basra; Operation Karbala-5 page), held until Iraq's Tawakalna 1 of 25 May 1988 (Tawakalna ala Allah Operations page). Three cells at 36.05-36.24 N, 45.14-45.37 E lie on the Sardasht-Mawat axis of Operation Karbala-10 (14-25 April 1987, an advance of 34 km into Iraq per the list of Iranian ground operations); the Karbala-10 page names Sulaymaniyah and Halabja instead and calls the gains 'Minimal territorial gains of insignificant lands for Iran', so the identification is my reading. The Iranian bridgehead at al-Faw (29.98 N, 48.47 E) is outside Cliopatria's cells. All the extra cells are gone in the 1990 shape, which agrees with the infobox 'Status quo ante bellum'.
1,624,310 km2, identical to the 1979 outline: after the ceasefire of August 1988 the war page records 'Status quo ante bellum' and no permanent border change.

1,624,554 km2: one cell (253 km2, at 39.3 N 45.0 E) more than 1990, on the frontier with the Azeri exclave of Nakhchivan. The Iran page names the new northern neighbours (Armenia, Nakhchivan and Azerbaijan to the northwest, Turkmenistan to the northeast) without dating them; the cell is a raster sliver of the new frontier, inside the precision of the era, and no territory changed hands.

1,624,652 km2 for 1996-2023: a second sliver cell (at 38.9 N 46.2 E) on the Armenian frontier beyond the 1990 outline. Infobox 1,648,195 km2, ratio 0.986. No border change is recorded by the page between 1996 and 2023.
Identical to the 1996-2023 shape; the Iran page records no territorial change in 2024.

region.text: Iranian Kurdistan: the province of Kordestan with Sanandaj, and the Mahabad district of West Azerbaijan

ledger.note: March 1979: the Kurdish rebellion begins as Kurdish forces seize towns in Iranian Kurdistan, before the republic is proclaimed on 1 April. 'In mid-March, Kurdish factions took control of police headquarters, army bases, and parts of army barracks in Sanandaj' and 'Kurdish militants, primarily from the KDPI, initially made territorial gains in Mahabad'; the rebels retook Mahabad on 20 October 1979 and 'By May 1980, Kurds still controlled most of Kurdistan's roads and rural areas and held Mahabad as their capital', until in the spring of 1980 government forces 'captured most of the Kurdish cities'. The zone is Kordestan plus a 30 km circle round Mahabad, my reading of the towns named (Paveh in Kermanshah and Piranshahr in West Azerbaijan, which the page also names as taken by the rebels in August-September 1979, lie outside it and are not drawn). The earlier version of this event cited the Kurdish separatism page, which gives no month and no town.

region.text: Iran, from the Caspian Sea to the Persian Gulf, as the Islamic Republic

ledger.note: 1979: Iran becomes an Islamic republic. 'On 31 March 1979, a referendum was held on whether to transition from a government of monarchy to an Islamic republic' and 'was approved by a massive margin of 99.31%'; the infobox gives 'Islamic Republic established: 1 April 1979' and 'Iranian Revolution: 11 February 1979'. The page gives no date for the Shah's departure and describes no separate proclamation.

region.text: Khuzestan, where four Iraqi divisions struck; the area bounded by Khorramshahr, Ahvaz, Susangerd and Musian; and the central front, where Iraq occupied Mehran and secured ground forward of Qasr-e Shirin

ledger.note: 1980: Iraq invades Iran. 'On 22 September 1980, the Iraqi army invaded Iran at Khuzestan' (Iran page); the war page has four divisions sent to Khuzestan, two besieging Abadan and Khorramshahr, and Iraq occupying Mehran on the central front. Iraq had already seized Zain al-Qaws and Saif Saad on 10 September; most of Khorramshahr was captured by 24 October 1980 (Iranian forces withdrew across the Karun). The page does not say Abadan fell.

region.text: the Shatt al-Arab and the border areas on both banks that Iraq meant to cut off and hold as a 'territorial security zone'

ledger.note: 1980: the Shatt al-Arab becomes the fighting line. The Iraqi plan was to cut off the Shatt al-Arab and set up a 'territorial security zone'; after June 1982 Iraqi troops 'continued to occupy some key Iranian border areas', notably the Shatt al-Arab. The zone is my reading of the river and its banks; the page gives no area (only a 644 km front).

region.text: Khuzestan, where four Iraqi divisions struck; the area bounded by Khorramshahr, Ahvaz, Susangerd and Musian; and the central front, where Iraq occupied Mehran and secured ground forward of Qasr-e Shirin

ledger.note: 1982: Iran retakes Khuzestan. Operation Beit ol-Moqaddas began in April 1982, the drive on Khorramshahr on 23 May 1982 and the city fell in under 48 hours, 19,000 Iraqis surrendering; Iran 'recaptured all their territory by June 1982', although Iraqi troops kept some border areas on the Shatt al-Arab. On 20 June 1982 Saddam offered a ceasefire and withdrawal from Iranian land; the page does not say it was completed.

1982: the Kurdish rebellion ends. the rebellion 'ended in December 1982, with 10,000 killed and 200,000 displaced' (the same page also says more than 30,000 Kurds died in the 1979 rebellion and the consequent KDPI insurgency, and does not reconcile the two). A later KDPI insurgency ran 1989-1996 with no land held. The 1979 Kurdish rebellion page, opened for the start, dates the rebellion 'March 1979-1983' in its infobox and says 'Clashes in the area continued until 1983'; the December 1982 end is kept because the Kurdish separatism page states it, and the pages disagree by up to a year.

region.text: the Iraqi town of Haj Omran

ledger.note: 23 July 1983: Iran takes the Iraqi town of Haj Omran. 'With Kurdish support, the Iranians attacked on 23 July 1983, capturing the Iraqi town of Haj Omran'; the page says Iran held it despite an Iraqi counteroffensive with poison gas, and that Operation Dawn 4 later in the year 'gained some of its former territory, as well as some Iraqi land' (15 km into Iraq). The Haji Omaran page puts the town in Erbil Governorate about 20 km east of Choman and gives no coordinates, so the 25 km circle at 36.65 N, 45.05 E clipped to Iraq is my reading, the same ground iraqi-republic.json /ledger/7 records for the other side. Added after review; the first version of this dossier missed it.

region.text: Majnoon Island in the Hawizeh Marshes

ledger.note: 1984: Iran takes Majnoon Island. In Operation Kheibar (24 February to 19 March 1984) through the Hawizeh Marshes, Iranian forces captured Majnoon Island 'By 27 February' and kept it after an Iraqi counterattack pushed them back from the outskirts of Qurna; the aim was the Basra-Baghdad highway, which Iran never held. The earlier region was a 90 km circle round Basra, which also hatched Basra, Khorramshahr, Abadan and northern Kuwait; it is replaced by a 25 km circle on the island (31.05 N, 47.55 E; the Majnoon Field page puts the field 60 km from Basra) clipped to Iraq. A second page (the list of Iranian ground operations) gives Kheibar's gain as Majnoon Island, 160 km2, with about 50 oil wells.

region.text: the tip of the al-Faw peninsula, from the Shatt al-Arab to the Khor Abdullah opposite Kuwait

ledger.note: 1986: Iran crosses the Shatt al-Arab and takes al-Faw. Operation Dawn 8 began on 9 February 1986 with an amphibious assault; the tip of the peninsula was overrun in about 24 hours, the town held out until 14 February, about 20,000 Iranian troops crossed on pontoon bridges and Iran reached the Khor Abdullah, about 16 km from Kuwait. Infobox: 'Iran captures the tip of the al-Faw peninsula' (10 February to 10 March 1986). The earlier region was the whole Iraqi bank of the Shatt al-Arab within 30 km, which also hatched Basra and the river up to Qurna; the page has Iran only on the tip of the peninsula ('Iranian troops succeeded in reaching the Khor Abdullah waterway opposite Kuwait') and a feint at al-Qurnah that 'was stopped by the Iraqis'. The 25 km circle on Al-Faw (29.976 N, 48.472 E on the Al-Faw page) clipped to Iraq is the fix.

region.text: Iraqi ground east of Basra at Fish Lake and the Jasim canal, no nearer than about 15 km to the city

ledger.note: 8 January 1987: Operation Karbala-5 (the Siege of Basra) opens and Iran takes ground east of Basra. The page has the operation begin at midnight on '8 January 1987', Iran crossing Fish Lake and taking the Duayji canal as a bridgehead, driving the Iraqis back over the Jasim river and coming within 15 km of the city, after which Iraq counterattacked and contained the Iranians to the Shalamjah area; the operation 'officially ended by the end of February' but the trench war continued. The region is my reading of those places (the page gives no coordinates); Cliopatria's 1987 shape carries six cells there (30.64-30.98 N, 47.70-48.07 E, about 1,517 km2), a wider strip than the circle.

region.text: the Iraqi side of the Sardasht-Mawat axis, about 34 km deep into Iraqi Kurdistan

ledger.note: 14 April 1987: Operation Karbala-10 carries Iran and the PUK Peshmerga into Iraqi Kurdistan. 'Following the failure of the Siege of Basra, the Iranians launched Operation Karbala 10 in northern Iraq on 14 April'; the page says they took 'the outskirts of Sulaymaniyah and Halabja and lands around them' and its infobox says 'Minimal territorial gains of insignificant lands for Iran'. The list of Iranian ground operations (second page) puts it on the Baneh-Sardasht-Mavout axis, 14-25 April 1987, an advance of 34 km into Iraq that stalled at the Shakh Qoolan heights; the pages disagree on the place, and the circle at 36.15 N, 45.30 E is my reading, chosen because Cliopatria's 1987 shape has three cells at 36.05-36.24 N, 45.14-45.37 E, 34 km west of Sardasht. No page says whether the ground was held.

region.text: the tip of the al-Faw peninsula, from the Shatt al-Arab to the Khor Abdullah opposite Kuwait

ledger.note: 1988: Iraq retakes al-Faw. Operation Ramadan Mubarak, 17-18 April 1988: Faw town fell about 35 hours into the attack and within 48 hours all Iranian forces had been 'killed or cleared' from the peninsula; infobox 'Iraqis liberate the Al-Faw peninsula'.

region.text: Iraqi ground east of Basra at Fish Lake and the Jasim canal, no nearer than about 15 km to the city

ledger.note: 25 May 1988: Iraq clears Iranian forces from the front east of Basra. 'At 9:30am on 25 May 1988, Iraq launched what became known as Tawakalna 1': 'Iraqi forces attacked Iranian positions at Fish Lake, at a point east of Basra', drove across the Jassem canal on the Basra-Khorramshahr road and 'cleared a 15-mile corridor'. The page does not say that nothing remained east of the corridor; its infobox has 'Iraqi forces regain control over all Iraqi territory previously held by Iranian forces'.

region.text: Majnoon Island in the Hawizeh Marshes

ledger.note: 25 June 1988: Iraq retakes Majnoon Island. 'On 25 June, Iraq launched the second Tawakal ala Allah operation liberating Majnoon Island.' A second page (Operation Forty Stars) says Iraq 'did claim that its forces had recaptured the oil-rich Majnoun islands' at the end of that week. This replaces the earlier ceasefire placeholder (confidence 1), which the pages opened then could not date.

region.text: the Iranian towns of Dehloran (Ilam) and Qasr-e Shirin taken by Iraq in July 1988

ledger.note: July 1988: Iraq occupies Iranian land at Dehloran and Qasr-e Shirin (recorded with the roles reversed: the land is Iran's, the occupier is Iraq). 'By 12 July at the central front' the Iraqis 'captured the city of Dehloran and Qasre Shirin', and the infobox has 'Renewed Iraqi invasion of Iran, resulting in the capture of dozens of towns (occupying 9,600sq.km)'; the page adds Sumar, Naft Shahr, Sarpol Zahab, Saleh Abad, Mousiyan and Patak, which are not drawn. Dehloran lies at 32.689 N, 47.269 E in Ilam Province (Dehloran page); the Second Battle of al-Faw page says it was 30 km inside the border. Mehran was taken on 18 June 1988 by the MEK/PMOI with Iraqi forces, who 'left the area after three days' (Operation Forty Stars page), and is not drawn. The 30 km circles are my reading.

region.text: the Iraqi town of Haj Omran

ledger.note: By 12 July 1988: Iraq has cleared its territory of Iranian forces, Haj Omran among it. The infobox has 'Complete elimination of Iranian forces in Iraq (liberating 4,400sq.km)' and 'Iraqi forces regain control over all Iraqi territory previously held by Iranian forces', and the text has Iraq 'in control of virtually all of the Iranian positions on its territory' within hours of 12 July; the page does not name Haj Omran, so the month is the latest the page supports. The war page gives 'Status quo ante bellum' and a ceasefire 'effective in August 1988'.

region.text: the Iraqi side of the Sardasht-Mawat axis, about 34 km deep into Iraqi Kurdistan

ledger.note: By 12 July 1988: the Karbala-10 strip is bridged to the same sweep (confidence 1). No page opened names the ground or says when Iran left it; the Tawakalna page's infobox says Iraq regained 'all Iraqi territory previously held by Iranian forces', and Cliopatria's 1990 shape has none of the 1987 northern cells.

region.text: the Shatt al-Arab and the border areas on both banks that Iraq meant to cut off and hold as a 'territorial security zone'

ledger.note: 1988: the ceasefire ends the fighting on the frontier. The infobox dates the war 22 September 1980 to 20 August 1988 with the result 'Inconclusive' and 'Status quo ante bellum'; Khomeini accepted a UN-mediated truce (Iran page: 'drank the cup of poison').

region.text: the Iranian towns of Dehloran (Ilam) and Qasr-e Shirin taken by Iraq in July 1988

ledger.note: August 1988: Iraq withdraws from the Iranian towns after the ceasefire. 'soon after Khomeini's acceptance of the UN ceasefire deal on 20 July 1988' the page has the Iraqis withdraw 'from the towns, claiming that they had no desire to conquer Iranian territory'; it gives no day, so the month follows the ceasefire that took effect in August 1988 (war page; 20 August in its infobox).

wars.name: Iran-Iraq War

zones.text: Khuzestan, where four Iraqi divisions struck; the area bounded by Khorramshahr, Ahvaz, Susangerd and Musian; and the central front, where Iraq occupied Mehran and secured ground forward of Qasr-e Shirin
the Shatt al-Arab and the border areas on both banks that Iraq meant to cut off and hold as a 'territorial security zone'
Majnoon Island in the Hawizeh Marshes
the tip of the al-Faw peninsula, from the Shatt al-Arab to the Khor Abdullah opposite Kuwait
the Iraqi town of Haj Omran
Iraqi ground east of Basra at Fish Lake and the Jasim canal, no nearer than about 15 km to the city
the Iraqi side of the Sardasht-Mawat axis, about 34 km deep into Iraqi Kurdistan
the Iranian towns of Dehloran (Ilam) and Qasr-e Shirin taken by Iraq in July 1988

wars.outcome: Inconclusive; 'Status quo ante bellum'. Iraq invaded Khuzestan on 22 September 1980 and held Khorramshahr from October 1980 to May 1982; Iran recaptured its territory by June 1982, took Haj Omran (July 1983), Majnoon Island (February 1984), al-Faw (February 1986) and ground east of Basra (January 1987), lost al-Faw (April 1988), the Fish Lake front (25 May 1988) and Majnoon (25 June 1988), and by 12 July had no force left in Iraq; Iraq took Dehloran and Qasr-e Shirin in July 1988 and withdrew after the UN-brokered ceasefire effective August 1988 (20 August in the infobox).
wars.note: The war page gives no occupied areas in km2, only a 644 km front, and its land narrative stops in 1984 (86,594 characters returned); 1985-1988 on land comes from the al-Faw, Karbala-5, Karbala-10, Tawakalna and Forty Stars pages and the list of Iranian ground operations. The Majnoon and al-Faw zones were redrawn after review (the first versions covered Basra); Dawn 4 is dated September 1983 on the war page and 19 October-21 November 1983 (Penjwen, about 700 km2) on the list page, and is not drawn.

wars.name: First Battle of al-Faw

zones.text: the tip of the al-Faw peninsula, from the Shatt al-Arab to the Khor Abdullah opposite Kuwait

wars.outcome: Iranian victory (Operation Dawn 8, 9 February to March 1986): Iran captured the tip of the al-Faw peninsula and held it, with clashes until the end of 1986 and as late as 1988.
wars.note: Infobox 10 February to 10 March 1986; the operation table says 9-25 February.

wars.name: Second Battle of al-Faw

zones.text: the tip of the al-Faw peninsula, from the Shatt al-Arab to the Khor Abdullah opposite Kuwait

wars.outcome: Iraqi victory on 17-18 April 1988 (Operation Ramadan Mubarak): the peninsula was cleared of Iranian forces within 48 hours; Iraq's last offensive then took Dehloran, about 30 km inside Ilam province (the page gives no date).
wars.note: The page is silent on the withdrawal of Iraq from Iranian land after the ceasefire. The Tawakalna ala Allah Operations page dates the Iraqi capture of Dehloran and Qasre Shirin 'By 12 July' 1988 and their evacuation 'soon after' 20 July 1988; they are ledger events here.

wars.name: 1979 Kurdish rebellion

zones.text: Iranian Kurdistan: the province of Kordestan with Sanandaj, and the Mahabad district of West Azerbaijan

wars.outcome: The rebellion led by the KDPI and Komala in Iranian Kurdistan 'ended in December 1982'; the page gives 10,000 killed and 200,000 displaced (and elsewhere over 30,000 dead).
wars.note: The Kurdish separatism page gives no town and no control date; the 1979 Kurdish rebellion page (opened later) names Sanandaj and Mahabad (March 1979), Paveh, Saqqez, Marivan, Baneh and Piranshahr (July-October 1979), Kurdish control of Mahabad into 1980 and the government's recapture of most Kurdish cities in spring 1980, and dates the rebellion 'March 1979-1983'.

certainty.note: The frontiers are treaty and survey lines (the war page names the 1975 Algiers Agreement, which ceded the eastern bank of the Shatt al-Arab to Iran, and the status quo ante bellum of 1988). Exceptions: the front lines of 1980-1988 (Khuzestan, the Shatt al-Arab, Haj Omran, Majnoon, al-Faw, Fish Lake east of Basra, the Sardasht-Mawat axis and the Dehloran-Qasr-e Shirin salient of July 1988) are not borders and are drawn by contest and occupation events; Iranian Kurdistan 1979-1982 is a rebellion zone; the Abu Musa and Tunb islands and the Caspian boundary were not checked (the Iran page is silent).

sources.title: Iran

Silent on the Shah's departure date, Abu Musa and the Tunbs, the Kurdish insurgency and the dates of the new republics.

Re-read for the repair: Haj Omran (23 July 1983), Majnoon ('By 27 February'), the ceasefire 'effective in August 1988'; silent on Karbala-5 and on 1988 apart from 'In mid-1988, Iraq launched a series of counter-offensives'.

notes: Built from five pages in the first run (the budget) and repaired after review with ten more; the repair is the reason the page count exceeds the budget. Settled: the founding (referendum 31 March 1979, republic 1 April 1979), the Iraqi invasion and its reversal (September 1980 to June 1982), Haj Omran (23 July 1983), Majnoon (24 February 1984 to 25 June 1988), al-Faw (9 February 1986 to 17-18 April 1988), the Karbala-5 ground east of Basra (8 January 1987 to 25 May 1988), the sweep of Iraq by 12 July 1988, Iraq's capture of Dehloran and Qasr-e Shirin (by 12 July 1988) and the ceasefire (August 1988; 20 August in the infobox). Review repairs: the al-Faw and Majnoon regions were circles that covered Basra and Iran's own Khorramshahr and Abadan and are now 25 km circles on the places clipped to Iraq; the Haj Omran occupation (and its mirror in iraqi-republic.json /ledger/7 and /ledger/9) was missing from the ledger although the war page dates it. Keyframes 1983 and 1987 stay adjust: Cliopatria's shapes carry five and nine extra cells beyond the 1979/1990 outline; the six east of Basra in 1987 are the Karbala-5 gains and the three at 36.05-36.24 N, 45.14-45.37 E match the Karbala-10 advance of April 1987 (34 km on the Sardasht-Mavout axis) by my reading, the Karbala-10 page itself naming Sulaymaniyah and Halabja; the four cells east of Basra in the 1983 shape match no page. Not settled: (1) the Kurdish rebellion's end: December 1982 on the Kurdish separatism page, 'March 1979-1983' and 'Clashes in the area continued until 1983' on the 1979 rebellion page; the contest is kept to December 1982; the insurgents need a dossier (type rebel) since the 1979 page shows them holding Sanandaj, Mahabad and other towns in 1979-1980. (2) Operation Dawn 4: September 1983 on the war page, 19 October-21 November 1983, Penjwen, about 700 km2 of Iraqi land on the list page; not drawn. (3) Mehran (taken 18 June 1988 by the MEK/PMOI with Iraqi forces who left after three days) and the small towns of Sumar, Naft Shahr, Sarpol Zahab, Saleh Abad, Mousiyan and Patak are not drawn; the Tawakalna page's '9,600sq.km' is more than the two circles at Dehloran and Qasr-e Shirin cover. (4) Iran-held Abu Musa and the Tunbs (UAE claim), the Caspian boundary and the Aras and Turkmen frontiers after the Soviet dissolution: the Iran page is silent, nothing recorded. (5) Cliopatria's 1992 and 1996 shapes add one and two sliver cells on the Armenian and Nakhchivan frontier; judged raster noise. (6) Cross-dossier: iraqi-republic.json lacks the al-Faw occupation (1986-2 to 1988-4), the Karbala-5 and Karbala-10 grounds and Iraq's own 1988 occupation of Dehloran and Qasr-e Shirin, and dates the Majnoon and Haj Omran endings to 1988-8 where the Tawakalna page gives 25 June and 'by 12 July'. Rulers: the Supreme Leader list is from the Iran page (Khomeini December 1979; Khamenei named by the Constitutional Reform Council on Khomeini's deathbed in 1989; Ali Khamenei assassinated 28 February 2026 and Mojtaba Khamenei elected 8 March, both after the map's last year). Counterpart slugs without a dossier yet: iranian-kurdish-insurgents. Names the gazetteer lacks, used through coordinates: Al-Faw (29.976 N, 48.472 E), Majnoon Island (31.05 N, 47.55 E), Haj Omran (about 36.65 N, 45.05 E), Dehloran (32.689 N, 47.269 E), Fish Lake (about 30.8 N, 48.0 E); Paveh and Piranshahr are named in the notes only.
